text: For real parameters $A,B,C,x_0$, the Vinogradov bound for $E_{\pi^*}$ means that $E_{\pi^*}(x)\leq A(\log x)^B\exp\!\left(-C\frac{(\log x)^{3/5}}{(\log\log x)^{1/5}}\right)$ for every real $x\geq x_0$.
scope: This is a definition of a bound predicate, not an assertion that suitable constants exist. The parameters A, B, C and x₀ and the variable x are real. The quantified range is exactly every x ≥ x₀; there are no additional positivity hypotheses on A, B, C or x₀. The real functions and operations have the total conventions of the cited vocabulary, including exceptional inputs; no implicit restriction x₀ > 1 or x₀ ≥ 2 is imposed.

text: For a real variable $x$, $\pi(x)$ is the number of primes at most $x$ (and is zero for $x<0$). The Riemann prime-counting function is $\pi^*(x)=\sum_{k\geq 1}\pi(x^{1/k})/k$. The offset logarithmic integral is $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$.
scope: Definitions of the counting functions and the offset logarithmic integral used in the main statement; the real functions use the conventions of the cited vocabulary.
